Reference board · Round 1 · 23 November 2026

Luxury real estate one-pager, Ibiza and Mallorca

Eight references grouped into four candidate directions, plus three sites that show what the category normally looks like. Every screenshot was captured from the live site in this session. The styling of this board is not a proposal for the site.

How to read it. Values marked Measured were read from the rendered page at 1440px; Estimated values are judged from the screenshot. Only home pages were inspected. Motion and hover behaviour were not observed unless stated. Select any screenshot to enlarge it.

Category baseline: what to rise above

Three agencies active on the islands open the same way: an aerial or pool photograph, a search box, and a claim about the size of the portfolio.

This is useful for a portal and wrong for us. With four to six homes there is nothing to search, and the buyer we want is choosing an adviser, not filtering a database.

Engel & Völkers Ibiza

Search box, pool photograph, “Find your dream property”. Lower down: dense cards with price, beds and square metres, and a managing partner in a suit.

Balearic Properties

Drone shot of a turquoise bay, centred search, “more than 2,000” properties. Cookie bar left in view; it stayed on every frame.

Baerz & Co

Aerial city photograph with a brown wash, serif headline, search field. First-pass capture only; the second capture timed out.

Direction

Gallery White

The page behaves like a gallery wall: white ground, small quiet type, and photographs framed as objects with air around them.

Fit with the brief. Closest to “quiet, assured”. The risk is anonymity: with stand-in photography and no strong type, it can read as any architect’s site.

Domus Nova

domusnova.com · Live site · estate agency, London and Ibiza · Found via: Web search (Ibiza agencies; Blakstad result linked to its design directory) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

The only direct competitor that already behaves like a design studio. A centred, letter-spaced wordmark, then one framed interior with the next slides peeking in from both edges.

Typography
A soft light serif for headings at a modest 32px, grotesque for everything else. Nothing shouts; hierarchy comes from position, not size.
Imagery
Interiors with colour and character, shot straight-on. No drones, no pools in the opening frame.
Composition
Image centred at roughly 60% of the width with neighbours cropped at the edges, caption split left and right beneath it. Listings sit in a single row of small cards.
Colour
White and near-black text; all colour comes from the photographs.
Interaction
The hero is a carousel (adjacent slides visible). Its motion was not observed.

Principle worth taking

Frame the photograph, do not fill the screen with it. A caption split into “name” and “one-sentence character” is a strong listing pattern for a page with only 4–6 homes.

What would not transfer

The interiors are commissioned and distinctive. With stand-in images the frame draws attention to exactly what we have least of.

Moredesign

moredesign.es · Live site · architecture studio, Mallorca · Found via: Web search (Mediterranean architecture studios) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

Extreme restraint: a monogram, a line of three words, and a two-column grid of photographs with tiny grey captions. The architecture does all the talking.

Typography
Very small grey sans (14px) used for everything. No display type at all.
Imagery
Stone, lime plaster, timber, still water; warm low light. This is the Balearic material palette the brief is after.
Composition
Narrow content column (about 50% of a 1440px screen) with wide margins. Two equal columns, slightly uneven vertical rhythm.
Colour
Off-white ground rgb(252,252,252); mid-grey text. Colour entirely from stone and vegetation.
Interaction
None observed.

Principle worth taking

The image vocabulary: materials and light instead of views and pools. Narrow column with generous margins reads as confidence.

What would not transfer

Grey 14px text fails comfortable reading and is borderline for AA contrast. And a site with no voice cannot persuade anyone to enquire; an architect can afford that, an agency cannot.

Blakstad

blakstadibiza.com · Live site · architects and design consultants, Ibiza · Found via: Web search (Ibiza architecture) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

Gallery white with a voice: a large classical serif headline and a founder’s quotation set over the photograph. The whitewashed finca wall is treated as the brand itself.

Typography
Cormorant at 85px for the headline; a letter-spaced sans in capitals for labels. The pairing is a familiar “heritage” formula.
Imagery
White cubic architecture against deep blue sky; shadows as graphic shapes (C1).
Composition
Offset pairs: text block top-left, image lower-right, with a lot of empty white between them.
Colour
White, sky blue and grey text. The blue is in the photographs, not the interface.
Interaction
Hero is a crossfading slideshow (two frames visible blended in C3).

Principle worth taking

White wall plus blue sky plus hard shadow is the most specific “Ibiza” image there is, and it is not a cliché of the property category. A single quotation can carry the agency’s point of view.

What would not transfer

Cormorant with wide-tracked capitals is now the default “luxury” type pairing; using it would undo the distinctiveness.

Direction

Almanac

The agency presents itself as a publication: a literary serif with italics, tinted paper-coloured blocks, homes given titles instead of reference numbers.

Fit with the brief. Carries personality through type and colour, so it survives modest photography. Needs good writing, which we control.

Inigo

www.inigo.com · Live site · estate agency for historic homes, UK · Found via: Recalled, then opened and verified in this session · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

An estate agency that reads like a literary magazine. Each home gets a title in italic Caslon (“Wind in the Willows”), and the page moves through blocks of muted paper colours.

Typography
Caslon throughout, with a large italic for titles laid across the join between photograph and colour block. A small grotesque only for utility text.
Imagery
Two photographs per home: the exterior in context and one interior detail, at different scales.
Composition
Split hero: photograph left, flat colour right holding a smaller inset photograph, title bridging both. Listings in a strict three-column row with price and tenure in a two-line caption.
Colour
Warm grey ground, slate blue block, dusty pink band for editorial. Colour separates kinds of content.
Interaction
Not observed.

Principle worth taking

Give each home a name and a sentence, not a spec sheet. Use two or three tinted grounds to give a single page distinct chapters. Set titles across image edges.

What would not transfer

The palette is English and overcast; ours needs to be sun-bleached. The “Almanac” journal behind it is real editorial output we will not have.

White Ibiza

white-ibiza.com · Live site · island guide and magazine, Ibiza · Found via: Web search (Ibiza architecture and design coverage) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

A masthead. The name set very large in widely spaced capitals on white, with a single landscape photograph beneath it, like a magazine cover.

Typography
One narrow geometric sans; display in capitals with very wide tracking. Category headings in a small serif with short descriptions (E2).
Imagery
One coastal landscape, cropped wide, sitting under the masthead instead of behind it. Small drawn icons above categories.
Composition
Type first, image second: the wordmark occupies the top half of the screen on white. Four-column text row below.
Colour
Black on white with a pale peach band; “Issue 12” label reinforces the publication idea.
Interaction
A newsletter pop-up appeared on scroll (excluded from the evidence).

Principle worth taking

Lead with the name as a masthead and keep the photograph separate from the type, so text is always on a clean ground and always legible. Proof that an Ibiza brand can be black-on-white and still feel of the island.

What would not transfer

It is a guide with many categories; its lower page is a directory, which a one-page agency site should not imitate.

Direction

One Colour

A single saturated ground and a single typeface in capitals. The brand is an attitude before it is a catalogue.

Fit with the brief. The most memorable and the most “sunlit”, the least “quiet”. A €2m+ buyer may read it as hospitality, not as a trusted adviser. One reference only.

Hotel Corazón

www.hotelcorazon.com · Live site · hotel, Tramuntana, Mallorca · Found via: Web search (Wallpaper* coverage of Mallorca hotels) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

Everything is red. One saturated ground, one typeface in capitals, dark brown instead of black, and a close-up film of sunburnt skin instead of a view of the building.

Typography
A single display sans in capitals for navigation, manifesto and labels alike. A whole paragraph is centred in capitals (F2).
Imagery
Sensory close-ups, film grain, terracotta interiors that match the interface colour. The place is conveyed by temperature, not by architecture.
Composition
Centred, symmetrical, poster-like. Rooms in a tight grid with labels on the image.
Colour
Red ground with dark brown text and a darker brown header bar. Two colours do everything.
Interaction
Hero is a video player with visible controls. A full-width “Book now” bar is the first element.

Principle worth taking

One confident colour drawn from the place (terracotta, sunburn, bougainvillea) can do more than any amount of gold. Dark brown instead of black keeps everything warm. The enquiry action can be the first thing on the page.

What would not transfer

Paragraphs in centred capitals are hard to read, and the red-brown pairing fails contrast for body text. The tone is playful hospitality; property buyers need to trust us with seven figures.

Direction

Full-Bleed Cinema

The image fills the screen and the interface almost disappears: small white capitals over film or photography.

Fit with the brief. Depends entirely on exceptional footage or photography. With stock or generated images this is the direction most likely to look generic.

Camper & Nicholsons

www.camperandnicholsons.com · Live site · yacht brokerage · Found via: Web search (Awwwards luxury category, Honorable Mention listing) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

A broker for the same buyer, selling by atmosphere. Dark sea fills the screen; a few words in small white capitals sit at the left edge; the interface is nearly invisible.

Typography
One geometric sans. Headlines are only about 38px in capitals; the smallness against a huge image is what reads as expensive.
Imagery
People and water, not products: legs on a deck, a swimmer at the bow. Dark, saturated, cinematic.
Composition
Full-bleed image per section with a short text block pinned left; then an abrupt cut to a plain white section.
Colour
Deep sea green-black with white text; white sections with black text.
Interaction
Not observed. The opening frame showed open water with almost no content (G3).

Principle worth taking

Sell the life, not the asset: a human moment in each image. A short statement with one link is enough per screen. Small type can be the luxury signal.

What would not transfer

This is a production budget, not a layout. Without footage of this quality the direction collapses into a stock hero. The dark palette also points away from “sunlit”.

Le Collectionist

www.lecollectionist.com · Live site · luxury villa rental · Found via: Web search (Tatler article on luxury home rental sites) · Captured 2026-11-23 · Inspected: home page, desktop and mobile

The polished mainstream of the category next door: landscape hero with a search bar, then tabbed rows of homes and three tiers of service on white.

Typography
One geometric sans in capitals with a condensed display face for the hero word. Body text light and small.
Imagery
Seasonal landscape hero, then conventional interior thumbnails.
Composition
Hero occupies about half the screen so the first row of homes is visible without scrolling. Centred section titles, three-column rows.
Colour
White with black; colour from photography only.
Interaction
Search form in the hero; tabbed collections. A cookie panel covered part of a lower frame (excluded).

Principle worth taking

A shorter hero that lets the homes show in the first screen is good for a buyer who wants proof quickly. “Collections” is a neat way to group very few homes.

What would not transfer

Competent but interchangeable. It is the look a concept piece needs to rise above, and search-led layouts make no sense for six homes.

Your choice

Recommendation (a proposal, not a decision)

Almanac as the base, with the framing of Gallery White and one colour borrowed in spirit from One Colour. Type and writing carry the personality, which is what we fully control on a concept with stand-in imagery. Photographs are framed and captioned as in Domus Nova, never used as a full-screen background. The tinted grounds are re-tuned from Inigo’s overcast greys to sun-bleached tones, with a single warm earth colour doing the work Corazón’s red does.

I would leave Full-Bleed Cinema out: it is the direction that most depends on footage we do not have.

Tell me which references you like and what specifically in each: type, layout, imagery, colour or tone. Mixing is welcome, for example “the italic titles from Inigo, the masthead from White Ibiza, the materials photography from Moredesign, less colour than Corazón”. Tell me what you dislike too.
